field.name: writeArtifact content write keeps the Signoff history
field.type: On a content write whose prior head has at least one meta.lifecycle.signoffs entry and whose next head has no lifecycle or one with no signoffs: when the content CHANGED, the stored lifecycle is the default draft with the prior Signoff entries carried; when the content is UNCHANGED and the next head has NO lifecycle, the prior lifecycle is kept exactly as it is and no draft lifecycle is synthesized; approval and review are never carried through a change
field.purpose: A content write stores the next head's lifecycle, so re-authoring an artifact in signoff stores either no meta.lifecycle or a fresh draft lifecycle with signoffs [], and its Signoff history is lost. The history names the request a revision must be pushed to; without it a resubmission opens a second request. The content write already carries meta.tracker and meta.envelope forward; this keeps the Signoff history the same way, and for unchanged content keeps the whole prior lifecycle because no lifecycle step reaches draft from in-signoff or changes-requested, so a synthesized draft would throw.

body.rationale: Confirmed by running writeArtifact over a head with one Signoff entry: a next head with no lifecycle left the file with none, and a fresh draft lifecycle reset signoffs to []; the daemon review showed that a synthesized draft for unchanged content would throw IllegalTransitionError (lifecycle.ts:170). The change is additive and acts only when the prior head has a Signoff entry, so a repo with no signoff behaves as today.
